facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] **External input — existence of the Conway coefficient invariants.** T. Garaev, *Elementary proof of existence of the Alexander-Conway polynomial*, arXiv:2012.03086v1 (5 December 2020), Section1, Theorem1, PDF p.2, with the equivalence and skein charts on p.1, supplies a sequence $c_{-1}=0,c_0,c_1,\ldots$ of invariants of oriented link diagrams with unordered components. They are invariant under all oriented Reidemeister moves and planar isotopies, have $c_0(U)=1$ and $c_j(U)=0$ for $j>0$, and satisfy
$$c_j(L_+)-c_j(L_-)=c_{j-1}(L_0),\qquad j\ge0.$$
This is an imported established coefficient-existence result, not a claim to reconstruct its Reidemeister-III argument. The source's crossing sign agrees with the declared convention: it is positive when the ordered over/under tangent pair has positive planar determinant. Its Figure2 is the oriented smoothing in this Definition. Polynomial finiteness, integrality and uniqueness are earned below rather than falsely attributed to the coefficient-sequence statement alone.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] **External input — ambient-link interpretation and conventional normalization.** Chmutov–Duzhin–Mostovoy, *Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants*, §1.2.1, printed p.11/PDF19, gives the Reidemeister diagram criterion with its oriented extension; §2.3.1, printed pp.35–36/PDF43–44, states the Conway invariant of ORIENTED LINKS with values in $\mathbb Z[t]$, normalized to one on the unknot and satisfying its displayed positive-minus-negative skein relation. It uses links with unnumbered components. These are the ambient-link interpretation and the standard skein convention of [F1]; the letter $t$ is renamed $z$. The book's §2.3.2 expressly notes that existence is nontrivial. Here existence is EXTERNALLY supplied, not inferred from that observation or from a formal definition. The empty link, if included in the ambient link domain, is assigned the separate conventional zero value in the Definition; the imported skein characterization is only for nonempty links.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External input — perfect pairing and sewing.** BHMV, Theorem1.4 p.887, property(F) on p.886, Proposition1.9 p.891, and Theorem4.11 p.909: in this even-root theory the radical quotient is finite free with unimodular dual pairing, the admissible spine states form a basis with unit diagonal norms in the double pairing, and the universal gluing maps satisfy the TQFT axioms. Proposition1.9 permits the complementary handlebody giving $S^3$, rather than assuming the self-double and $S^3$ pairings have the same matrix. Their normalization is the $Z_p$ normalization explicitly fixed in [F1]. Only perfectness/basis/sewing at this actual convention is imported.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] **External input — actual weighted variant.** Gilmer–Masbaum, arXiv:0912.4706v3, §2 equation(1) pp.4–6 and §11 pp.23–25, states the colored TQFT with Lagrangians and integer weights and one-weight multiplier $\nu=\kappa^3$ in BHMV notation. The finite sign comparison $\mu_{GM}=-\mu_{Wall}$ is as recorded in the Kirby lemma, so its composition is exactly that of [F3]. The source states rational Lagrangians. For the real Lagrangians of [F3], take the rational handlebody-kernel reference on each marked surface and transport by the weight-zero identity cylinder to its specified real Lagrangian; the reverse cylinder is its inverse because $\mu(L,L',L)=0$. Conjugating morphisms by these cylinders is a functor to the rational-reference category, with the integer weights computed by [F3], so the imported functor extends to these real objects. This is a finite categorical transport, not an assumption that every real Lagrangian is rational.

facts.label: F5
facts.text:
[F5] **External input — actual BHMV Kirby color and Gauss units.** BHMV, *Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket*, Topology34(1995), §2 p.897, the displayed definition of $\theta_p$ and equations(*)–(**), together with §5.8 p.913: for the primitive $2p$-th root and even $p=2r$, the Kirby element is $\Omega_p=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_jp_j$ and
$$\Delta_\varepsilon=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{3\varepsilon}\quad(\varepsilon=\pm1),\qquad \eta\in\mathbb C^\times.$$
Here $\kappa$ is the selected BHMV SIXTH root from [F4], not the square-root weight parameter used by some later sources. The source's usual signed quantum dimensions are exactly $d_j=[j+1]$ for the registered negative-loop recurrence. Its recalled invariant $\theta_p(S^3(L))=\langle L(\Omega_p)\rangle/(\Delta_+^{b_+}\Delta_-^{b_-})$ includes the actual Kirby handle-slide identity. This established identity is imported, not claimed as a new local recoupling proof.

facts.label: F6
facts.text:
[F6] **External input — weighted normalization and exact sign.** BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum, arXiv:0912.4706v3, §2 pp.4–6 and §11 pp.23–25, give the weighted version. Put $
u=\kappa^3$; one weight step multiplies the map by $
u$. The closed TQFT normalization is $Z_p(M,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}
u^w	heta_p(M)$, componentwise with the banded data. It is this additional normalization, not raw $	heta_p$ alone, that supplies the finite TQFT. Gilmer–Masbaum's Maslov form on $(L_1+L_2)\cap L_3$ is $(a_1+a_2)\odot(b_1+b_2)=\omega(a_2,b_1)$. Modulo its radical it is the negative of the registered Wall form $\omega(a,b')$ with $a+b+c=0$. Thus their correction $-\mu_{GM}$ is precisely the registered $+\mu_{Wall}$. Their square-root parameter is $
u$, explicitly the cube of BHMV's parameter. No choice of an unrelated square root $\mathcal D_p$ is silently identified with $\eta^{-1}$; only $\mathcal D_p^2=\eta^{-2}$ follows.

facts.text: [F2] [[thm-local-existence-uniqueness-and-smooth-dependence-for-manifold-integral-curves]]: the geodesic ODE has local solutions and smooth dependence on initial data, so parallel frames and exponential-coordinate maps vary smoothly along an embedded geodesic subsegment.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **External input:** Dos Santos Ferreira--Kurylev--Lassas--Salo, Proposition 3.1, PDF p. 14, supplies exactly the residual, norm, and attenuated ray limit in the statement on an oriented compact transversal of dimension at least two. Its finite Taylor-jet construction and distinct-branch cross-term estimate (equation (3.6), PDF pp. 21--22) are imported, including overlap matching at self-intersections. For this repair the proposition and the cross-term argument on pp. 21--22 were inspected; the entire proof on pp. 14--22 is not claimed as newly reconstructed. Historical source coverage is distinct from this reading extent.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The construction for each fixed $K$ uses finitely many charts, finite Taylor orders, and linear transport and matrix ODEs with fixed initial data. Increasing the finite order suffices for that $K$; no simultaneous choice of quasimodes for unrelated $K$ or $\lambda$ is required. The parameter $\tau$ then enters the resulting explicit formula. Thus the use here adds no choice axiom to the statement.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The four-factor supplier uses the external smooth harmonic-product density theorem, Lassas--Liimatainen--Lin--Salo, Proposition 5.1, PDF p. 14 (source hypotheses: compact oriented CTA manifold of dimension at least three, $C^1$ coefficient, four or more smooth harmonic factors). Its actual witnesses are smooth on $\overline M$, depend on the coefficient being tested, and are constant in $\tau$. Thus the smooth-boundary identity [F2] applies directly; no extension of that identity to arbitrary $H^1$ boundary traces is required. The source statement and Section 5 through p. 20 were inspected, not the entire proof through p. 22. Theorem 1.3, pp. 5--6, is the corresponding nonlinear uniqueness theorem, not a replacement local proof here.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] **External input:** Lassas--Liimatainen--Lin--Salo, Proposition 5.1, arXiv:1903.12562v1, PDF p. 14: on a compact oriented transversally anisotropic manifold of dimension at least three, if $f\in C^1(M)$ satisfies $\int_M f v_1\cdots v_m\,dV=0$ for all smooth harmonic $v_j$, with $m\ge4$, then $f=0$. We import this density statement. The statement and proof through PDF p. 20 were inspected; the remaining proof through p. 22 is not claimed read or reconstructed here. The simple surface is diffeomorphic to a disk, hence oriented, so its product and $M$ meet the source orientation hypothesis.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] The literal quantifiers in the statement permit the four witnesses to depend on $Q$. They impose no uniformity in $Q$, no nonzero-solution requirement, and no quantitative remainder or beam-profile estimate. The proof below uses density to obtain smooth witnesses constant in $\tau$; it does not assert a uniform Gaussian-beam family. The Gaussian calculation fixes the allowed positive geometric normalization.

facts.label: F1
facts.text: [F1] [[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain]]: $g=dx_1^2\oplus g_0$ and $\Delta_g=\partial_{x_1}^2+\Delta_{g_0}$.

facts.label: F2
facts.text: [F2] [[lem-ip-limiting-carleman-estimate-on-product]]: for $\varphi=x_1$, the conjugated operator $P_{\varphi,h,q}=e^{\varphi/h}h^2(-\Delta_g+q)e^{-\varphi/h}$ has a distributional right inverse on $L^2$ with norm at most $C h^{-1}$.

facts.label: F3
facts.text: [F3] [[def-riemannian-gradient]] and [[def-laplace-beltrami-operator-as-trace-of-the-hessian]]: the product metric extends the gradient bilinearly to complex phases, and $\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g$.

facts.label: F4
facts.text: [F4] **External input:** Dos Santos Ferreira--Kurylev--Lassas--Salo, Proposition 2.1 (PDF p. 10), for a compact oriented CTA manifold, bounded potential, either sign of sufficiently large real $\tau$, and arbitrary $f\in L^2$, gives $r\in H^1$ solving $e^{\tau x_1}(-\Delta_g+q)e^{-\tau x_1}r=f$, with $\|r\|_{H^\alpha}\le C|\tau|^{\alpha-1}\|f\|_2$ for $0\le\alpha\le1$, with no prescribed boundary value. We import this statement, not a reconstructed shifted Carleman proof. Its statement and the application in Propositions 2.1--2.2, PDF pp. 10--11, were inspected; the older Proposition 4.4 citation issue is not treated as a local proof.

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] The orientation restriction in [F4] is removed for scalar equations by the orientation double cover of $M_0$. Lift $M,q,f$ to its product cover, solve there, and average the solution with its deck transform. The invariant solution descends to $H^1(M)$ and solves the original equation. The degree-two factors in the squared $L^2$ norms cancel in the estimate; the same applies to the local Sobolev norms. A disconnected cover is handled componentwise, using only finitely many choices.
